lines: Ethiopian civil conflict, Persecution of Christians in Ethiopia The Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church reports that at least 60 Christians have been killed in attacks in Oromia, Ethiopia, over the last week. (Reuters)
Nigerian bandit conflict The casualty toll from the massacre by unknown gunmen four days ago in Taraba State, Nigeria, increases to 62 people killed and 52 more wounded. (AP)
United States strikes on alleged drug traffickers during Operation Southern Spear The United States launches an airstrike against an alleged drug boat in the Caribbean Sea, killing five people. (AP)
Colombian conflict A bomb explodes near a bridge in Cúcuta, Colombia, at the border with Venezuela, injuring four police officers. (AP)

Eurovision Song Contest 2027 Netherlands in the Eurovision Song Contest 2027 Netherlands Public Broadcasting (NPO) withdraws the Netherlands from the 2027 Eurovision Song Contest over concerns about Israel's participation, after AVROTROS withdrew in August and NPO failed to find another broadcaster. (AP)

2026 North Indian Ocean cyclone season Indian authorities order nearly 100,000 people to evacuate parts of Andhra Pradesh and Odisha as Cyclone Arnab approaches, with the India Meteorological Department forecasting landfall as a very severe cyclonic storm. (AFP via RFI)
Four people are killed, two are missing and several homes are destroyed during floods in Haiti and the Dominican Republic. (AP)
A construction site is hit by a tornado in Kepez, Antalya, Turkey, killing four workers and injuring another. (AP)

2025 in climate change The World Meteorological Organization reports that global concentrations of carbon dioxide, methane, and nitrous oxide reached record highs in 2025, with carbon dioxide averaging 426.8 parts per million. (AFP via France 24)

Immigration to Nigeria Nigerian police arrest 34 foreigners, including 16 Cameroonians and 18 Nigeriens, suspected of engaging in "illicit activities" in Benue State. The commissioner opens an investigation into their immigration status. (Daily Trust)

Brazilian senator Flávio Bolsonaro leaves Brazil for the United States, despite orders to surrender his passports to the Federal Police, two days after his defeat in the presidential election runoffs to incumbent president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. The government subsequently cancels his passports. (Reuters)
2026 Israeli legislative election Israelis vote to elect the 120 members of the Knesset. (BBC News) (Reuters)
